title: Paired lore+quest hardening (OPAG-453): dash-led scope token (F4) and Unicode format characters passing the sanitiser (F5)
description: Routed by opum-agent OPAG-453 (orchestrator 94d64804, 2026-09-26T19:43:37Z), found by quest-cli's reviewer in code byte-identical to lore-cli dc09ca98 (LCLI-592). Ruling (d) keeps the two CLIs byte-identical here: quest-cli PROPOSES the change and lore-cli agrees it; a string or shape both repositories agree binds without the orchestrator. F4: the Claude scope token /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/ accepts a dash-led value, so a scope of '--scope' reaches both the printed remedy and argv. lore-cli has ALREADY tightened this to /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/ in LCLI-593 (opum-ai/lore-cli#297, head 235b3fe0, src/core/agent-plugins.ts; the adversarial review reproduced '--scope --help' through a stub), matching OPAG-453's proposed regex exactly. Only parity confirmation with quest-cli remains. F5: stripAnsiAndControls (src/errors.ts, which strips ANSI plus C0/C1 only) passes Unicode format characters: RLO U+202E, which reorders a printed line, and ZWSP. It must also strip U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069, U+200E, U+200F, U+061C, U+200B-U+200D, U+2060 and U+FEFF. OPEN SCOPE POINT, for agreement with quest-cli before implementing: in lore, stripAnsiAndControls is the single shared sanitiser (LORE-181) used by 8 source files (check, query, replace, output, validate and links messages among them), not only plugin text. Extending it changes every sanitised output, and stripping U+200D (ZWJ) splits emoji ZWJ sequences in document titles or ids that lore query and check print. Settle with quest-cli whether the shared helper carries the full set, or runtime-sourced text gets it while ZWJ is kept for document text. Record the agreed choice here.

acceptanceCriteria.text: F4: the dash-led scope rejection is on lore-cli dev (via LCLI-593) and confirmed byte-identical in shape to quest-cli's fix, citing both SHAs

F5: the ONE shared sanitiser (stripAnsiAndControls, no two-mode split) additionally strips exactly U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069, U+200B, U+2060 and U+FEFF, and KEEPS U+200C, U+200D, U+200E, U+200F and U+061C (emoji ZWJ, Persian/Indic ZWNJ, RTL marks); proven by tests including an RLO that would reorder a printed line and positive controls that each kept character survives, byte-identical in rule to quest-cli QCLI-382 (OPAG-453 ruling, narrowed 2026-09-26T19:48:58Z)
The parity is cited: lore-cli's implementing SHA and quest-cli's are exchanged (via opum-agent while quest-cli is being renewed); bun test and bun run lore check exit 0

implementationNotes: RULED 2026-09-26T19:48:58Z by opum-agent (orchestrator 94d64804), recorded on OPAG-453, which settles this record's OPEN SCOPE POINT: ONE shared helper, with no two-mode split. stripAnsiAndControls strips ONLY U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069, U+200B, U+2060 and U+FEFF in addition to today's ANSI and C0/C1, and KEEPS U+200C, U+200D, U+200E, U+200F and U+061C because they carry meaning in legitimate text (emoji ZWJ, Persian and Indic ZWNJ, RTL marks). This narrows OPAG-453's original list. quest-cli is amending QCLI-382 to match.

F4, verified 2026-09-26: origin/dev src/core/agent-plugins.ts:126 carries /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/ (from LCLI-593, opum-ai/lore-cli#297), the OPAG-453 regex exactly. quest-cli QCLI-382 matches that regex. The SHA exchange is still owed (AC1). F5 IMPLEMENTED on fix/LCLI-607-unicode-format-strip: stripAnsiAndControls (src/errors.ts) gets a third pass that removes /[‪-‮⁦-⁩​⁠﻿]/g, one shared helper with no two-mode split. U+200C, U+200D, U+200E, U+200F and U+061C are kept. Tests in test/errors.test.ts, "stripAnsiAndControls — Unicode format characters (LCLI-607, OPAG-453 F5)": an RLO line; each of the 12 stripped code points; each of the 5 kept ones as positive controls; a ZWJ emoji sequence plus a ZWNJ Persian word; an exact-set sweep over U+0600-06FF, U+2000-206F and U+FE00-FEFF; and a caller (stderrHint). MUTATIONS, predicted from the test file: removing the pass turns exactly 15 red (RLO, 12 stripped, sweep, caller) and all 5 kept controls stay green; widening the class to U+200B-U+200D turns exactly 4 red (keep 200C, keep 200D, emoji/Persian, sweep). Gates: bun test 3666 pass / 0 fail, bun run lore check 0 errors, typecheck clean. PARITY: quest-cli had not yet proposed QCLI-382 code (not on its dev; no open PR, read 2026-09-26). lore offered this exact class to quest-cli to adopt or counter under ruling (d), and the PR does not merge until they agree.

PARITY AGREED 2026-09-26 by quest-cli (cross-session message, session quest-cli [b2a6a5]): F5 is byte-for-byte the class in lore source f2d3223c src/errors.ts:206, /[‪-‮⁦-⁩​⁠﻿]/g written with \u escapes, as a third pass after the ANSI and C0/C1 strips; this matches QCLI-382 narrowed set exactly. F4 agreed: /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/. quest-cli will send its implementing SHA once QCLI-382 comes up in its ruled order (after QCLI-384), and it cleared #307 to merge on this agreement. quest-cli measured a layering note: JS \s matches U+FEFF, and both CLIs collapse /\s+/ to a space in plugin printable() before the sanitiser runs, so on that path a FEFF prints as a space. lore pins FEFF removal at the stripAnsiAndControls level (test/errors.test.ts), which is the right layer. Ordering check: lore notRunDetail tests managed before the bare-call and disabled branches, so no other detail reaches a managed row. AC2 (F5) is checked on this agreement with the tests and mutations recorded above. AC1 and AC3 stay open until quest-cli sends its SHA; this task is then closed in the PR that records it.
